name: Atlantic Salmon
description: Anadromous fish known for their incredible upstream migrations to spawn.
funFact: Can leap up to 3 meters (10 ft) out of water to clear waterfalls.

name: West Indian Manatee
description: Gentle herbivorous marine mammals often called 'sea cows'.
funFact: Manatees are more closely related to elephants than to whales or dolphins.

name: Bottlenose Dolphin
description: Highly intelligent cetaceans famous for complex social structures and echolocation.
funFact: Dolphins sleep with one eye open and half their brain awake at a time.

name: Striped Bass
description: Prized silvery fish with distinct dark horizontal stripes along its flanks.
funFact: Can live in both freshwater rivers and open coastal saltwater.

name: Polar Bear (Max Dive)
description: The largest land carnivore can dive down to 30 meters while hunting seals underwater.
funFact: Polar bear fur is translucent and hollow, not white; it reflects visible light.

name: Giant Kelp Forest
description: One of the fastest-growing organisms on Earth, forming underwater cathedral forests.
funFact: Can grow up to 60 cm (2 feet) in a single day under ideal sunlight conditions.

name: Great White Shark
description: Apex predator of the open oceans equipped with electromagnetic sensing ampullae.
funFact: Can detect a single droplet of blood in 100 liters of water from kilometers away.

name: Great Barracuda
description: Fierce torpedo-shaped predator capable of explosive bursts of speed up to 58 km/h.
funFact: Drawn to shiny metallic reflections because they resemble fish scales.

name: Killer Whale (Orca)
description: The ocean's ultimate apex predator, possessing distinct dialect cultures between pods.
funFact: Despite their name, killer whales are the largest members of the dolphin family.

name: Giant Oceanic Manta Ray
description: The world's largest ray, gliding effortlessly through the water like an underwater bird.
funFact: Has the highest brain-to-body mass ratio of all cold-blooded fish.

name: Green Sea Turtle
description: Graceful marine reptiles that navigate thousands of miles across oceans using geomagnetic sense.
funFact: Can hold their breath underwater for up to 5 hours while resting or sleeping.

name: Whale Shark
description: The largest known extant fish species, filter-feeding peacefully on microscopic plankton.
funFact: Their skin is covered in unique constellation-like white spots as distinct as human fingerprints.

name: Firefly Squid
description: Tiny bioluminescent cephalopod that illuminates Toyama Bay, Japan, with sparkling blue lights.
funFact: Uses counter-illumination photophores on its underside to camouflage against sunlight from above.

name: Sea Angel
description: Translucent swimming sea slug with wing-like parapodia, fluttering gracefully through cold waters.
funFact: Despite their angelic look, they are voracious predators of sea butterflies, tearing them from their shells.

name: World Record Scuba Dive
description: Deepest open-circuit scuba dive by a human in history, set in Dahab, Egypt.
funFact: The descent took just 15 minutes, but the decompression return to the surface took nearly 15 hours!

name: Shortfin Mako Shark
description: The fastest shark in the world, capable of swimming bursts of up to 74 km/h (46 mph).
funFact: Can leap up to 9 meters (30 feet) clear into the air when chasing fish.

name: Emperor Penguin (Max Dive)
description: Can dive to incredible depths exceeding 500 meters in freezing Antarctic oceans.
funFact: Their bones are solid rather than hollow, reducing barotrauma under extreme hydrostatic pressures.

name: Chambered Nautilus
description: A 'living fossil' unchanged for 500 million years, with an exquisite logarithmic spiral shell.
funFact: Controls its buoyancy by pumping gas and liquid through tiny chambers inside its shell via a siphuncle.

name: Ocean Sunfish (Mola Mola)
description: One of the heaviest known bony fish in the world, resembling a giant swimming fish head.
funFact: Female sunfish can produce up to 300,000,000 eggs at once — more than any other vertebrate.

name: Japanese Spider Crab
description: Possesses the largest leg span of any arthropod on Earth, reaching up to 3.8 meters claw to claw.
funFact: Can live to be over 100 years old on the deep muddy continental shelf.

name: Coelacanth
description: Thought to have gone extinct 66 million years ago with the dinosaurs until rediscovered alive in 1938.
funFact: Has unique paired lobed fins that move in an alternating diagonal pattern, exactly like four-legged land animals.

name: Barreleye Fish
description: Has a transparent, fluid-filled shield on its head through which its glowing green tubular eyes rotate.
funFact: The two dark spots above its mouth that look like eyes are actually nares (olfactory organs).

name: Megamouth Shark
description: Extremely rare filter-feeding shark discovered only in 1976 when one entangled an oceanographic anchor.
funFact: Has a luminous band around its mouth believed to attract plankton into its cavernous jaws in the dark.

name: Giant Pacific Octopus
description: The largest octopus species in the world, with three hearts, blue blood, and incredible problem-solving intellect.
funFact: Has approximately 2,240 suction cups across its eight arms, each packed with taste receptors.

name: Burj Khalifa Comparison
description: The tallest building and freestanding structure on Earth would be completely submerged here.
funFact: At this depth, you are deeper than the highest human inhabited floor in the sky.

name: Deep Sea Hatchetfish
description: Ultra-thin, silver-scaled fish with upward-gazing tubular eyes and belly photophores.
funFact: Its body is so laterally compressed it is virtually invisible when viewed head-on.

name: Sperm Whale
description: The largest toothed predator on Earth, plunging a vertical kilometer down to battle giant squids.
funFact: Produces the loudest biological sound on Earth — clicks reaching 230 decibels, enough to stun prey.

name: Humpback Anglerfish
description: Icon of the abyss with needle teeth and a bioluminescent dorsal spine lure (illicium) filled with glowing bacteria.
funFact: Males are dwarfed parasites that bite onto females, permanently fusing their bloodstreams and flesh.
size: Females up to 20 cm, males 3 cm

name: Vampire Squid
description: Translates to 'vampire squid from hell', with crimson webbing resembling a Dracula cloak.
funFact: Not a true squid or octopus, but the sole surviving member of its own ancient cephalopod order.

name: Sloane's Viperfish
description: Has teeth so monstrously large and needle-sharp they cannot fit inside its mouth and curve past its eyes.
funFact: Holds the Guinness World Record for the largest teeth relative to body size of any living fish.

name: Slender Snipe Eel
description: Possesses a bird-like curved beak lined with thousands of microscopic hook-like teeth to snag shrimp antennae.
funFact: Has up to 750 vertebrae in its spine — more than any other vertebrate animal on Earth.
size: Up to 1.5 meters, yet weighs only ounces

name: Phronima (Alien Amphipod)
description: Deep sea hyperiid amphipod that was the biological inspiration for the Xenomorph Queen in the movie 'Alien'.
funFact: Attacks gelatinous salps, eats their insides, and hollows out their transparent barrel body to live and lay eggs inside.

name: Blobfish
description: At natural deep-sea pressures, it looks like a normal sculpted fish; it only melts into a 'blob' when pulled to the surface.
funFact: Lacks a swim bladder because gas chambers would implode under 160 atmospheres of crushing hydrostatic pressure.

name: Goblin Shark
description: Ancient pink-skinned lineage dating back 125 million years, with an elongated dagger-like snout.
funFact: Can shoot its jaws forward at 3.1 meters per second to snap up prey in a fraction of a heartbeat.

name: Halitrephes Jellyfish (Firework)
description: Radial hydromedusa that explodes into a dazzling starburst of radiant colors under ROV submersible lighting.
funFact: In the pitch-black abyss, without human artificial sub floodlights, this glorious firework is completely invisible.

name: Giant Isopod
description: Enormous deep sea crustacean cousin of the common garden pillbug, adapted to scavenging ocean floor carcasses.
funFact: A captive giant isopod in a Japanese aquarium went over 5 continuous years without eating a single bite of food.

name: Southern Elephant Seal (Record Dive)
description: The deepest diving carnivoran mammal on Earth, recorded down to an astonishing 2,388 meters.
funFact: Can store huge quantities of oxygen in their muscles using myoglobin and slow their heart rate down to 4-10 bpm.

name: Gulper Eel (Pelican Eel)
description: Has a cavernous pelican pouch maw that unfolds like an umbrella to engulf prey much larger than itself.
funFact: Its tail terminates in a complex bioluminescent organ that glows with pink and red bioluminescent flashes.

name: Bigfin Squid (Magnapinna)
description: One of the most ghostly, alien-like organisms in the ocean, with 8-meter elbowed tentacles trailing beneath it.
funFact: First filmed by deep-sea ROVs near oil rigs, floating motionless in the crushing void.

name: Black Swallower
description: Capable of swallowing prey over twice its length and more than ten times its own mass whole.
funFact: Its stomach expands so enormously that the prey fish's tail coils visibly inside its translucent belly.

name: Cuvier's Beaked Whale
description: The reigning champion diving marine mammal of planet Earth, holding the record at nearly 3,000m.
funFact: Can hold its breath for an astounding 3 hours and 42 minutes during extreme deep foraging dives.

name: Wreck of the RMS Titanic
description: The resting place of the legendary ocean liner that sank on April 15, 1912, after colliding with an iceberg.
funFact: Halomonas titanicae, a rust-eating extremophile bacterium, is steadily consuming the ship's 50,000 tons of iron.

name: Giant Squid
description: Deep sea titan with eyes the size of basketballs (27 cm) — the largest eyes in the animal kingdom.
funFact: First recorded alive in its natural deep habitat only in 2004 by Japanese marine scientists.

name: Carnivorous Harp Sponge
description: Resembles an ornate candelabra or musical harp, anchored into abyssal mud to snag passing prey.
funFact: Unlike shallow filter sponges, this abyssal creature is a ruthless carnivore, digesting trapped crustaceans with enzymes.

name: Mount Everest (Submerged Marker)
description: If Mount Everest (8,849 m) were placed at the bottom of the Mariana Trench, its summit would still be under 2,000m of water!
funFact: The ocean's deepest abyss is over 2,000 meters deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

name: Dumbo Octopus
description: Charming abyssal cephalopod that flaps two prominent ear-like fins resembling Disney's Dumbo.
funFact: Lives deeper than any other known octopus, happily thriving under pressures that would crush a submarine.

name: Sea Pig
description: Plump pink deep-sea holothurian (sea cucumber) that marches across the abyssal plains on hydraulics-powered tube feet.
funFact: Often gather in massive herds of hundreds of individuals, all facing in the exact same ocean current direction.

name: Hydrothermal Black Smoker Vent
description: Geothermal geysers spewing mineral-rich water at over 400°C (750°F) that does not boil due to crushing pressure.
funFact: Forms the foundation for chemosynthetic alien ecosystems independent of the sun, feeding giant tube worms.

name: Tripod Fish
description: Perches atop the seabed using three elongated fin rays like a photographer's tripod, facing into the current.
funFact: Nearly blind; uses its specialized pectoral fins like sensory antennae to feel subtle vibrations of drifting prey.

name: Faceless Cusk
description: Bizarre abyssal fish with no visible eyes or distinct face, rediscovered in 2017 off the coast of Australia.
funFact: Its eyes are buried deep beneath its skin tissue, rendering them completely invisible from the outside.

name: DSV Alvin Submersible
description: The world's most famous deep-sea research vessel, having completed over 5,000 dives since 1964.
funFact: Explored the Titanic wreck in 1986 and discovered deep-sea hydrothermal vents in 1977.

name: Wreck of the USS Johnston
description: One of the deepest surveyed shipwrecks in human history, located in the Philippine Trench.
funFact: Surveyed in 2021 by Caladan Oceanic at a staggering depth of 6,456 meters (21,180 ft).

name: Hadal Grenadier (Rattail)
description: Large-headed, tapered-tail fish cruising silently above the trench floor to scavenge sinking detritus.
funFact: Utilizes high levels of TMAO (trimethylamine N-oxide) to protect cellular enzymes from being crushed by water pressure.

name: Abyssobrotula Galatheae
description: Once held the record for the deepest living fish ever dredged from the ocean floor, at 8,370m in the Puerto Rico Trench.
funFact: Lives in pitch darkness at temperatures barely above freezing, under hydrostatic pressures exceeding 800 atmospheres.

name: Mariana Snailfish
description: The deepest living fish verified on planet Earth! Translucent, pinkish, and completely dominant in the hadal trenches.
funFact: Biochemists have calculated that 8,400 meters is the theoretical physical limit for any fish with bones before proteins unravel.

name: Deepsea Challenger (James Cameron)
description: Film director James Cameron piloted this 24-foot vertical lime-green sub on a solo journey to Challenger Deep.
funFact: Spent 2 hours and 36 minutes traversing the bottom, describing the seabed as a 'bleak, lunar, alien desert'.

name: Bathyscaphe Trieste
description: First human vessel to ever reach the Mariana Trench, pioneering human deep-sea exploration.
funFact: The pressure sphere had walls 12.7 cm (5 inches) thick made of forged high-tensile Krupp steel.

name: Challenger Deep — Bottom of the Ocean
scientificName: 10,928 meters / 35,853 feet • Expedition by Sriya Vaishnavi Tinnavelli
description: The absolute deepest known point on planet Earth, located in the southern end of the Mariana Trench. Explored and conquered by Sriya Vaishnavi Tinnavelli.
funFact: The hydrostatic pressure here exceeds 1,086 bar (15,750 psi) — equivalent to the weight of an elephant balanced on a postage stamp.
